A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSM-Symbolic study. Their text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite reformatting and added appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 25 language models, including benchmark comparisons, perturbation experiments, prompting and fine-tuning ablations, and failure examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds arithmetic evaluations, statistical tests, and per-question conditional-correctness analyses.

M1.justification: The symbolic-template construction, validation checks, and benchmark-variant generation remain unchanged. The added numerical-range explanation documents the existing design; the new appendix analyses do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: The GSM8K and GSM-Symbolic variants are retained. Appendix A.6 adds isolated addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division questions, extending evaluation from mathematical word problems to a focused arithmetic task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same 25 models, and the prompting and fine-tuning comparisons in Figures 8 and 11 are unchanged. The added arithmetic analyses use previously evaluated models; newly cited studies are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The original 100-template, 50-instance, eight-shot evaluation settings remain intact. Appendix A.6 introduces zero-shot arithmetic tests with at least 1,000 cases per operation and answer-digit length, plus arithmetic-correctness evaluation of equations extracted from generated responses.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.6 directly investigates whether arithmetic difficulty explains the benchmark declines, combining digit distributions, isolated arithmetic tests, and generated-equation checks. Appendix B adds correctness analysis conditioned on solving the original question. These substantially extend the retained perturbation, prompting, and fine-tuning analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports distributions, means, and standard deviations. v2 adds two-sided one-sample t-tests, normality checks, and p-values in Figures 10 and 12, alongside conditional-probability analysis and explicit statistical assumptions. The original 50 generated evaluation sets remain unchanged; no increased run count is established.

E6.justification: Table 1's model scores and uncertainties are unchanged, but substantial supplementary results are added. Table 2 reports Gemma2-9b-it arithmetic accuracy of 98.9%, 98.3%, 97.4%, and 97.1% on GSM8K, GSM-Symbolic, GSM-P1, and GSM-P2 respectively. Figures 15–18 add digit statistics, arithmetic results, and conditional-correctness findings; Figures 10 and 12 add significance outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a formal conditional-correctness argument absent from v1: an ideal reasoner preserves success or failure under renaming, giving conditional success probabilities of one or zero and a total-score distribution with expected value 100 times p_m and zero variance. This is a limited new mathematical formalization.

C1.justification: The benchmark and reasoning-fragility contributions remain central. However, the abstract removes 'all' from the numerical-change performance claim, and the conclusion removes the prediction that limitations become more pronounced on harder mathematical benchmarks. These modestly narrow particular claims.

C2.justification: v2 argues from the new arithmetic controls that calculation difficulty is unlikely to explain the large performance declines. Appendices A.3 and B substantially expand qualifications: significance depends on statistical assumptions, an alternative analysis yields nonsignificance, and the ideal zero-variance argument excludes non-reasoning errors that can also affect humans.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link and availability statement for templates and generated data, absent from v1. It also documents numerical-range selection, arithmetic-probe prompts, and equation-extraction checks. These improve reproducibility information without establishing changes to the original experimental settings.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens the reasoning background and positioning, adding foundational AI literature and related intervention studies by Stolfo, Hong, and Srivastava, among others. Appendices A.3 and B also engage directly with Ivanova et al.'s statistical criticism, introducing a substantive new relationship to prior analysis.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are edited, Related Work becomes Background with expanded explanations, and Appendices A.6 and B are appended. Author affiliations and publication headers change. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact, so this is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting, changing typography, text width, and figure/table sizing and placement throughout. Figure 10 expands from three to nine panels, Figures 10 and 12 gain p-value annotations, and Figures 15–18 and Table 2 are added. Some added panels redisplay existing distributions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the arithmetic controls in Appendix A.6 address a concrete alternative explanation, while Appendices A.3 and B make statistical assumptions and conflicting interpretations more transparent. Added data-access information also helps reproducibility. These are useful gains, but significance remains assumption-dependent and the broad inference from performance fragility to absence of genuine reasoning remains unresolved.
